extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets. Heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by manual labeling by expert annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA datasets), puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic paper figures from Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answers to free-form questions (integers, floating-point numbers, or lists) were converted into a standard format to facilitate consistent accuracy evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates by filtering for numeric answers or quantity words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, and discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was analyzed using the Fleiss Kappa score, yielding a score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields and expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules for automatic filtration based on numeric answers and quantity words.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process with commitments to maintain the datasets, refine potential data noise based on community feedback, and evolve the leaderboard.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark facilitates the development of AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, which has applications in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include potential gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals, and annotations lacking a unified format and structure due to the heterogeneity of sources.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Model development validation and standard evaluation of mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts.
